description:
Create or update a Kubernetes resource via Server-Side Apply. The manifest is the complete desired state: any field this tool previously set and the new manifest omits is removed. To edit an existing resource, fetch it with resources_get, modify it, then re-apply the full resource.
(common apiVersion and kind include: v1 Pod, v1 Service, v1 Node, apps/v1 Deployment, networking.k8s.io/v1 Ingress, route.openshift.io/v1 Route)

context.description: Optional parameter selecting which context to run the tool in. Defaults to fake-context if not set

dry_run.description: Validate every document with a server-side dry run (admission, schema, field ownership) and write nothing. The result lists each document as the API would store it. A multi-document manifest is always validated this way before its first write.

force.description: Take over fields that other field managers own (server-side apply force). Default false: if the manifest sets a field another writer owns, nothing is written and the error names the fields and their managers, so a concurrent change is not silently reverted.

mode.description: 'apply' (default) creates the object or updates the fields it sets. 'create' only creates: an existing object of the same name is left untouched and the error names it and its field managers.

on_failure.description: For multi-document manifests, if a document fails after earlier ones were written: 'stop' (default) leaves the written ones and lists them; 'rollback' deletes the ones this call created. Objects that existed before are not restored. This is a compensating action, not a transaction: the result lists exactly what was rolled back and what was not.

output.description: What the result shows of each written object: 'receipt' (default) gives apiVersion, kind, namespace, name, uid, resourceVersion and generation; 'full' gives the whole object as stored, as earlier versions did.

resource.description: Complete YAML or JSON representation of the Kubernetes resource (full desired state, not a partial patch). Include apiVersion, kind, metadata, and the full spec.

name: resources_create_or_update
title: Resources: Create or Update

description:
Delete a Kubernetes resource in the current cluster by providing its apiVersion, kind, optionally the namespace, and its name
(common apiVersion and kind include: v1 Pod, v1 Service, v1 Node, apps/v1 Deployment, networking.k8s.io/v1 Ingress, route.openshift.io/v1 Route)

apiVersion.description: apiVersion of the resource (examples of valid apiVersion are: v1, apps/v1, networking.k8s.io/v1)

context.description: Optional parameter selecting which context to run the tool in. Defaults to fake-context if not set

dry_run.description: With labelSelector: list the objects that would be affected and change nothing.

gracePeriodSeconds.description: Optional duration in seconds before the object should be deleted. Value must be non-negative integer. The value zero indicates delete immediately. If this value is nil, the default grace period for the specified type will be used

kind.description: kind of the resource (examples of valid kind are: Pod, Service, Deployment, Ingress)

labelSelector.description: Instead of name: act on every object of this kind in the namespace whose labels match (e.g. 'cache=stale'). Must not be empty. Each object is handled on its own (best effort) and gets its own result line.

namespace.description: Optional Namespace to delete the namespaced resource from (ignored in case of cluster scoped resources). If not provided, will delete resource from configured namespace

propagationPolicy.description: What happens to dependents (for example a Job's Pods): Background (default, like kubectl delete) deletes them after the object, Foreground before it, Orphan leaves them.

resourceVersion.description: Optional precondition: the metadata.resourceVersion you read. The delete is refused if the object changed since.

uid.description: Optional precondition: the metadata.uid you read. The delete is refused if the object was deleted and recreated under the same name since.

name: resources_delete
title: Resources: Delete

context.description: Optional parameter selecting which context to run the tool in. Defaults to fake-context if not set

fields.description: Return only these fields, as dotted paths; [N] picks a list element and [*] every element, e.g. ["spec.template.spec.containers[*].resources.limits"].

kind.description: kind of the resource (examples of valid kind are: Pod, Service, Deployment, Ingress)

names.description: Instead of name: read several objects of this kind in one call; each object's error is reported inline.

namespace.description: Optional Namespace to retrieve the namespaced resource from (ignored in case of cluster scoped resources). If not provided, will get resource from configured namespace

description:
Add, change or remove labels on one object (name) or on every object of a kind that matches a label selector, without sending the objects. Other labels are left alone. With labelSelector each object is handled on its own (best effort) and gets its own result line.
(common apiVersion and kind include: v1 Pod, v1 Service, v1 Node, apps/v1 Deployment, networking.k8s.io/v1 Ingress, route.openshift.io/v1 Route)

apiVersion.description: apiVersion of the resources (examples of valid apiVersion are: v1, apps/v1, networking.k8s.io/v1)

context.description: Optional parameter selecting which context to run the tool in. Defaults to fake-context if not set

dry_run.description: With labelSelector: list the objects that would be labelled and change nothing.

kind.description: kind of the resources (examples of valid kind are: Pod, Service, Deployment, ConfigMap)

labelSelector.description: Instead of name: label every object of this kind in the namespace whose labels match (e.g. 'app=web'). Must not be empty.

labels.description: Labels to set, as key: value; a null value removes the label (e.g. {"tier": "cache", "stale": null})

name.description: Name of one object to label (or use labelSelector)

namespace.description: Optional Namespace (ignored for cluster scoped resources). If not provided, the configured namespace is used

(common apiVersion and kind include: v1 Pod, v1 Service, v1 Node, apps/v1 Deployment, networking.k8s.io/v1 Ingress, route.openshift.io/v1 Route)

all_kinds.description: Instead of apiVersion and kind: list every namespaced kind the cluster serves (except Events) in the given namespace, names only, leaving out kinds with no objects. Use it to see everything in a namespace, e.g. before or after a clean-up.

apiVersion.description: apiVersion of the resources (examples of valid apiVersion are: v1, apps/v1, networking.k8s.io/v1)

context.description: Optional parameter selecting which context to run the tool in. Defaults to fake-context if not set

continue.description: Opaque token from the continue field of the previous page. Send it unchanged with the same limit, namespace, and selectors to retrieve the next page. Omit on the first call.

fieldSelector.description: Optional Kubernetes field selector to filter resources by field values (e.g. 'status.phase=Running', 'metadata.name=myresource'). Supported fields vary by resource type. For Pods: metadata.name, metadata.namespace, spec.nodeName, spec.restartPolicy, spec.schedulerName, spec.serviceAccountName, status.phase (Pending/Running/Succeeded/Failed/Unknown), status.podIP, status.nominatedNodeName. See https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/field-selectors/

fields.description: Return only these fields of each object, as dotted paths; [N] picks a list element and [*] every element, e.g. ["spec.replicas", "spec.template.spec.containers[*].image"].

kind.description: kind of the resources (examples of valid kind are: Pod, Service, Deployment, Ingress)

kinds.description: Instead of apiVersion and kind: list several kinds in one call, e.g. [{"apiVersion":"apps/v1","kind":"Deployment"},{"apiVersion":"v1","kind":"Service"}]. Returns the names per kind, with each kind's error inline.

labelSelector.description: Optional Kubernetes label selector (e.g. 'app=myapp,env=prod' or 'app in (myapp,yourapp)'), use this option when you want to filter the resources by label

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return. Omit or set to 0 to list everything, which fails if the response exceeds max_backend_response_bytes. Retry with a smaller limit when that happens. The API may return fewer items than requested.

namespace.description: Optional Namespace to retrieve the namespaced resources from (ignored in case of cluster scoped resources). If not provided, will list resources from all namespaces

wide.description: Include the columns kubectl shows only with -o wide (for Pods: IP, Node, Nominated Node, Readiness Gates; for Deployments: Containers, Images, Selector) in the structured rows. Default false.

description:
Patch one Kubernetes resource, like kubectl patch: change, add or remove individual fields without sending the whole object. Use it for one-field edits, to remove a label, annotation or finalizer, or to delete a map key that another tool or person set (server-side apply cannot remove fields it does not own). Pass resourceVersion (from a read) to make the patch fail instead of overwriting a change made since.
(common apiVersion and kind include: v1 Pod, v1 Service, v1 Node, apps/v1 Deployment, networking.k8s.io/v1 Ingress, route.openshift.io/v1 Route)

apiVersion.description: apiVersion of the resource (examples of valid apiVersion are: v1, apps/v1, networking.k8s.io/v1)

context.description: Optional parameter selecting which context to run the tool in. Defaults to fake-context if not set

kind.description: kind of the resource (examples of valid kind are: Pod, Service, Deployment, Ingress)

namespace.description: Optional Namespace of the resource (ignored for cluster scoped resources). If not provided, the configured namespace is used

output.description: What the result shows of each written object: 'receipt' (default) gives apiVersion, kind, namespace, name, uid, resourceVersion and generation; 'full' gives the whole object as stored, as earlier versions did.

patch.description: The patch, as JSON or YAML

patchType.description: 'merge' (JSON merge patch, RFC 7386: an object; null removes a key), 'strategic' (built-in kinds only: merges lists by key, e.g. containers by name), 'json' (JSON patch, RFC 6902: an array of operations such as {"op":"remove","path":"/metadata/finalizers"})

resourceVersion.description: Optional precondition: the metadata.resourceVersion you read. The patch is refused with a conflict if the object has changed since.

name: resources_patch
title: Resources: Patch

namespace.description: Optional Namespace to get/update the namespaced resource scale from (ignored in case of cluster scoped resources). If not provided, will get/update resource scale from configured namespace

output.description: What the result shows of each written object: 'receipt' (default) gives apiVersion, kind, namespace, name, uid, resourceVersion and generation; 'full' gives the whole object as stored, as earlier versions did.

scale.description: Optional scale to update the resources scale to. If not provided, will return the current scale of the resource, and not update it
